channel.description: Latest articles from Peninsula Daily News (peninsuladailynews.com)

item.title: LETTER: Stop deforestation
item.description: Perhaps we can all agree that the state needs to manage our forests better, but certainly not by destroying them at a more rapid rate.

item.title: LETTER: Waiting for downfall
item.description: As our country begins its 250th anniversary yearn founded with the military acumen of George Washington and the ideals of Thomas Jefferson, both of whom became president in their 50s, we need to consider what to celebrate.

item.title: LETTER: Sheriff guidelines
item.description: Clallam County Sheriff Brian King recently opined against Senate Bill 5974. He considers it overreach by the state and declares it would undermine his authority. He would have you believe that his judgment alone should determine who could become a deputy.

item.title: GIRLS BASKETBALL PLAYOFFS (updated): Port Angeles and Sequim qualify for state
item.description: Wolves’ Chartraw scores 43 points in victory over Orting

item.title: Clallam County deputies investigating homicide
item.description: Sheriff’s office asks public for help with video surveillance

item.title: COLLEGE BASKETBALL: Peninsula College men, women both win heading into home finale
item.description: BREMERTON — The Peninsula College men’s basketball team did what it had to, winning two games it had to win to keep playoff dreams alive, while the Peninsula College women won another North Region championship thanks to a little help from Bellevue.

item.title: MAT CLASSIC WRESTLING: Forks’ Blair, Daman state champions
item.description: TACOMA — For the first time since 1992, the Forks wrestling programs have two state champions.

item.title: PREP PLAYOFF BASKETBALL: Port Angeles boys season ended by Franklin Pierce
item.description: BREMERTON — The Port Angeles boys came painfully close to qualifying for the state 2A tournament, but fell in the District 3 2A tournament in a tough one Saturday 48-44 to Franklin Pierce.

item.title: BOYS SWIM AND DIVE: Port Angeles fourth at state meet
item.description: Relay teams all place; Van Denburg, Jones shine

item.title: Class 1B BASKETBALL PLAYOFFS: Neah Bay boys, girls both to state
item.description: AUBURN — Both the Neah Bay boys and girls basketball teams are headed back to the state 1B tournament, with the Neah Bay girls winning another Tri-District championship as part of their quest to win four straight state championships.
